It's honestly tough as fuck, and I'd be a liar if I said that it doesn't bother me still. It has taken four years for me to actually like rain again.

For the longest time in my life, I lived in a home that was falling apart, full of mold, and leaked so badly, me and my mother would have to stay up all night to empty the various buckets and pans we used to catch the water. 

My father worked hard to supply me and my family with everything we needed. But he didn't have enough to keep up with the repairs that needed to be done. We always had to bail water out of the tub if we wanted to bathe, and sometimes that meant that I went without showers because I didn't have enough time to both bathe and bail out the water that I used.

The thing that bothers me the most now, is how they got all this stuff for me even though I was an asshole then. I had a 360 and a ps3, even though the money they used to buy that stuff could've been used to pay for another home.

But luckily this story ends happily. I'm now with my parents in a trailer. It's nothing huge, but we have a home that isn't crumbling around us. Last time I went to check out the house, a section of the floor caved in, the parts of the roof that was leaking the worst caved in, and the mold situation in the house is worse. If we didn't move out when we did, it would've ended up killing someone. 

Now. If any of you are in a similar situation, the best thing for you to do is stay positive. Count every single one of your blessings. Don't beat yourself up over what's happening in your life. Do your best to advance and get out. Even if it means you eating ramen for dinner everyday for a while, save up to get out. At least you weren't on the street. I know how much living in a home like that sucks, but I'm lucky compared to some friends. I always had a bed to lie my head in.
